# Agent Factory Lab

> Open research lab with 52 experiments testing techniques to make AI coding agents faster, cheaper, and more reliable.

This site documents research findings and experiment results for improving two AI coding agents: Gwaihir (orchestrator for herdr, a multi-agent coding tool) and Landroval (orchestrator for Rex, a coding factory).

## Key Results (37 real measurements, 15 simulated/estimated)

Real measurements:
- Batched tool calls: 94.5% token reduction, 90% fewer requests (tiktoken)
- Terse completions: 95.7% output token reduction (tiktoken)
- Prompt caching: 72.3% cost savings, break-even at turn 2 (tiktoken + pricing)
- HANDOFF.md: 53% token reduction, 100% fact retention (tiktoken)
- Parallel pane execution: 1.83x speedup (tmux)
- Mutation check: 100% kill rate on 10 mutations (pytest)
- Stop hook: blocks premature "done" on buggy code (pytest)
- Remote VM sessions: 100% survival across 5 disconnect cycles (tmux)

Additional real measurements (batch 3 — sandboxing):
- Bubblewrap OS sandbox: 6/6 tests pass, 3.4ms overhead (bwrap)
- Booby-trap scanner: 8/8 threats detected, all critical neutralized (git)
- Host-held secret placeholders: no leaks detected in synthetic examples (not a security guarantee)
- Step-log resume: completed steps skipped on resume represent 58% of modeled fresh-run tokens, not total crash+resume savings; retries can replay effects, requiring idempotency or external deduplication (not exactly-once)
- Snapshot/restore: sub-50ms restore for 20MB state (filesystem)
- Risk-routed sandbox: independent narrow checks only; no integrated routing or security validation
- TokenEconomizer: 643/644 offline tests pass; paper claims 18-31% cost savings (unverified by us)
- Anthropic message threads: 82.7% payload reduction over 30 turns (tiktoken); latency optimization, not cost
- AGENTS.md size check + repo root guard: 9/9 tests pass
- Verifier-only lane: 7/10 real accuracy (pytest), 96% fewer bad merges (Monte Carlo)
- Repo map before reads: 57% fewer tokens, 0 wrong-file opens (tiktoken)
- Cache-monotonic prefix linter: 87% cost savings clean vs dirty prefix (tiktoken)
- Status notes vs transcript re-reads: 93% token reduction for polling (tiktoken)
- Session dump/restore: state intact, 14ms restore (tmux)
- Pegboard config sync: 3 harnesses, 0 MCP drift
- Fresh reviewer: 3/5 correct approved, 4/4 adversarial caught (pytest)
- Generated handoff: 38.7% token savings, zero LLM calls (tiktoken)
- Fold-and-restore: 38% context reduction, 5/5 restorable vs 0/5 hard compaction (tiktoken)
- Eval gate (dsh-superagent reimpl): 96% of triggers filtered before LLM call (500-trigger stream)
- Structured reports: 70% fewer status-check tokens, deterministic routing (tiktoken)
- Subagent task-file spawn: 92% fewer tokens vs cloned history, all task files <400 tokens (tiktoken)
- Tokens/completed-task efficiency stack: 19% savings normally, 73% under failures (tiktoken + hashing)
- Mailbox implementer/reviewer protocol: 5/5 adversarial caught, 92% fewer tokens than self-review (pytest + tiktoken, reimplementation of agent-coordination)
- Pane input guard: 100% → 0% clobber rate, 4.7ms overhead (tmux)
- Blocking-only reviewer: 5/5 adversarial, 78% fewer comments, 0 style nits (pytest)
- Discovery token levers: 89% combined savings (quiet flags + trimmed config + summaries), diff guard catches AGENTS.md injection with 0 false positives (tiktoken + git)
- Combined-changes gate: 2 integration breaks caught (0 per-branch), 0.25s overhead (git + pytest)
- Stale-instruction checker: 100% precision/recall on 6 planted cases (pattern matching)
- MCP tool pruning: 53% savings upfront, 93% with caching over 20 turns (tiktoken)
- Needs-human queue: 50% message reduction, 100% precision/recall on needs-human detection (30 samples)
- Compact dashboard: 88% fewer tokens vs raw scrollback for 5-agent review (tiktoken)
- Proof-of-done gate: 4/4 false claims caught, 0 false flags, 160ms overhead (pytest)
- Skill budget: 15 skills fit in 1% context budget (433 of 2000 tokens) (tiktoken)

Simulated/estimated:
- Writer/reviewer pipeline: +15pp fix rate, -42% defect escapes (Monte Carlo)
- Agent races: 60% → 91% success rate at 3x cost (Monte Carlo)
- Cheap model routing: 20.9% cost savings (public pricing)
- Bug priority gate: 18% token savings, 0 high-severity bugs missed
- AGENTS.md single source: eliminates config drift (0 vs 6.5 rule gap)
- Reviewer scoring: F1=0.793 on synthetic corpus
- Capped review rounds: 5.2% token savings (needs harder scenarios)
- Correction-to-skill: 10 skills extracted from 150 corrections
- SuperPlane: 4/5 auto-shipped via risk-gated state machine
- Firecracker/Lizard cost model: bubblewrap 0.1%, microVM 2-7% overhead
- Per-second VM billing: 94% savings vs hourly
- forgerun local microVM: protocol documented (requires KVM)
- Handoff accept gate: eliminates silent discards, 100% wasted token reduction (Monte Carlo)
- Write/review router: 20-40% review cost savings (public pricing)
